findings.title: Rename route checks the 'read' permission instead of 'write', so read-only users and anonymous visitors can rename files
findings.evidence: `.post('/rename', ({ user, ip, body }) => { const a = need({ user, ip }, body.space, 'read')` then `moveSync(from, to)`. Every other route that changes files (mkdir, newfile, PUT content, copy, move, delete) requires 'write'. The default guestPermissions are ['read','download','batchdownload']. An anonymous visitor calls GET /api/session to get a cookie and CSRF token, then sends POST /api/rename {space:'public', path:'/report.pdf', name:'x.pdf'} with X-CSRF-Token and renames any file or folder in the public area. A user with read-only rights can do the same in their home or public space.

findings.title: Backup restore never asks for the admin password again
findings.evidence: `void body.password` followed by `const { safety } = await restoreBackup(body.name)`. confirmPassword() is never called, unlike /api/admin/update/apply and /rollback (`await confirmPassword(admin, ip, body.password, 'update-denied')`), and the README says restore needs the password. Anyone holding only an admin session cookie can send POST /api/admin/backups/restore {name:'file-center-backup-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.zip', password:'anything'} with the CSRF token. This replaces users.json (accounts and password hashes), settings and branding, restarts the app, and skips the step-up lockout.

findings.title: Copy-into-self guard is skipped when the folder name starts with '..', so one request can fill the disk
findings.evidence: `const rel = relative(from, to); if (!rel.startsWith('..') && !rel.startsWith(sep) && rel !== '') { if (within(from, to)) throw bad('files.copy-into-self') }`. validName and normRel only reject the exact name '..', so folders named '..a' and '..a/..b' are allowed. POST /api/copy {space:'home', items:['/..a'], dest:'/..a/..b'} makes rel = '..b/..a', which starts with '..', so the within() check never runs. copyTree then walks into the copy it is writing. It nests and re-copies every file in '..a' at each level until the path is too long (about 500 levels), and has no space check. A user with only 'write' can use up the disk for everyone.

findings.title: Folder copy has no free-space check, unlike upload, zip and unzip (MIN_FREE_SPACE is not enforced)
findings.evidence: `void treeStats` / `await copyTree(from, uniquePath(to))`. There is no ensureSpace(destAbs, size) before the copy, although the README says copy is refused when the disk would drop below MIN_FREE_SPACE, and /zip, /unzip and uploads all check. A user with 'write' (or a guest, if granted 'write' on public) can repeat POST /api/copy {items:['/big'], dest:'/'} until the disk is full, so other users' uploads, session saves and backups fail.

findings.title: copyTree follows symlinks inside the tree it copies (statSync instead of lstat) and can copy files from outside the storage root
findings.evidence: `const st = statSync(s); if (st.isDirectory()) { await mkdir(d); stack.push([s, d]) } else if (st.isFile()) await copyFile(s, d, FS.COPYFILE_EXCL)`. Only the top item is checked with lstat. Children are stat'ed through links, so a symlink inside a copied folder that points to /etc or another user's folder is copied as real data into the caller's space, which they can then download through POST /api/copy. The code says links are skipped. No route creates symlinks (unzip and upload write regular files only), so this needs a link already placed in storage, hence medium.

findings.title: Search follows symlinks (stat instead of lstat), so it lists file names outside the caller's root
findings.evidence: `const stats = await Promise.all(look.map(n => stat(join(dir, n)).catch(() => null)))`, then `entryOf(...)` checks `st.isSymbolicLink()`, which is never true for a stat result. Symlinked folders are reported as dirs and descended (`stack.push([join(dir, look[k]), e.path])`). GET /api/search?space=public&q=a (guests have 'read' by default) returns names, sizes and mtimes of files under any symlinked target outside the root. This needs a symlink already present in storage.

findings.title: Login lockout key uses the username as typed, but lookup ignores case, so changing case resets the lockout
findings.evidence: `const key = `${ip}|${username}`` while findUser compares `u.username.toLowerCase() === username.toLowerCase()`. confirmPassword lowercases its key, this one does not. POST /api/login {username:'Admin'}, {username:'aDmin'}, ... each gets its own 5-attempt counter, so with 2^5 case variants of 'admin' an attacker gets about 160 password guesses per lockout window from one IP instead of 5.
